title: Word Break
spaceBreakdown:
- unordered_set<string> dict: up to 1000 entries → O(m)  
- vector<char> dp (size n+1): → O(n)  
- not counted: input strings, returned bool
approach: Treat the string as a sequence of prefixes. A prefix is reachable if it can be split into dictionary words, and from any reachable prefix we try to extend it by every word that matches the next characters. Using a boolean array for reachable prefixes and a hash set for fast word lookup yields a linear‑time DP that is provably correct because every valid segmentation builds the string prefix‑by‑prefix.
hints:
When scanning the string from left to right, which indices could serve as the end of a correctly segmented prefix?  
s length is at most 300.

Use an **unordered_set** to test “does this word appear in the dictionary?” in O(1).  
For s = "leetcode", after confirming the prefix “leet” is reachable, the set tells us that “code” matches the next characters, so the whole string becomes reachable.

```
dp[0] = true
for i = 0 … n‑1
    if dp[i] is false continue
    for each word w in dict
        if s starting at i has prefix w
            dp[i + |w|] = true
return dp[n]
```

**Single character match** - the string consists of one letter that is present in the dictionary.  
`Input: "a", ["a"]` → `Expected: true`  
⚠️ Bug: forgetting to set dp[0]=true → returns false  

**No possible split** - the whole string cannot be formed from any combination.  
`Input: "cats", ["dog","cat"]` → `Expected: false`  
⚠️ Bug: checking only the first word in the dictionary → may return true for "cat"  

**Overlapping words** - two dictionary words share a prefix, and the correct split uses the longer one later.  
`Input: "applepenapple", ["apple","pen"]` → `Expected: true`  
⚠️ Bug: breaking after the first matching word without continuing the outer loop → returns false  

**Maximum length word** - a word exactly 20 characters long appears at the end of the string.  
`Input: "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa", ["aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"]` → `Expected: true`  
⚠️ Bug: using `substr(i, word.length())` with i+len exceeding string size → out‑of‑range error.

followUps.q: How would you modify the solution to return **all** possible segmentations (Word Break II)?
followUps.a: Perform the same DP to know which prefixes are reachable, then run a DFS/back‑tracking from the end, using memoization to avoid recomputing sub‑problems. The time becomes exponential in the number of segmentations, while the DP‑pre‑check stays O(n·L).

followUps.q: If |s| could be up to 10⁵ instead of 300, what changes are needed to keep the algorithm fast?
followUps.a: Build a Trie from the dictionary and, for each reachable index, walk the Trie character by character, stopping when the path ends. This keeps the inner loop bounded by the maximum word length, so the overall complexity stays O(n·L) with L ≤ 20, and memory stays O(m·L).

followUps.q: Suppose the input string arrives as a **stream** and you cannot store the whole string in memory. How can you decide segmentation?
followUps.a: Keep a sliding window of at most L characters and a queue of reachable positions (indices modulo L). When a new character arrives, update the window and check all dictionary words that could end at the current position using the hash set; if any matches a reachable start, mark the current position reachable. This uses O(L) extra memory and O(1) amortized time per character.
